text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- South Africa wins Kenyan Centenary Four Nations cricket tournament at the Nairobi Gymkhana Club, maintaining its series of outstanding sporting achievements.

- Kenya's Opposition Alliance demands a date for the next general election by the end of the year as a sign of transparency so that the ruling KANU party does not gain undue advantage over other political parties.
- Energy Minister Darius Mbela says Uganda's threat to disconnect power supply to Kenya is unnecessary as the latter is willing to discuss the contentious tariffs issue.
- Finance minister Musalia Mudavadi says the government is finding it difficult to service its huge external debt totalling over 359 billion shillings ($6.3 billion).
- Lonrho East Africa Chairman Mark Too calls for resignation of Agriculture Minister Simeon Nyachae and others for failing to solve the problems facing the agricultural sector.
- Ghost buster in coastal region town of Kwale unearths an assortment of objects including snail shells, rugs and buried bottles in an effort to save a school haunted by spirits.
- Mayor Dick Waweru discloses that Nairobi City Council owes its employees 520 million shillings in salary arrears.

- Tests conducted by the Agriculture Ministry on wheat brought into Kenya from India, including a 14,000-tonne consignment impounded at the port in Mombasa, shows it carries "Karnal Burnt" fungus, which causes huge losses and compromises grain quality.
- A summit meeting of regional heads of state in Arusha this week will decide whether to lift or ease sanctions against Burundi.
- A stubborn effort by merchants to boycott Value Added Tax seems doomed to failure in the face of divisions amongst their own ranks and solidarity by government.
